newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Opposition battle police in Belgrade centre.
newsitem.headline: Opposition battle police in Belgrade centre.

text.p: Serbian riot police fired tear gas and used batons against opposition supporters in the centre of Belgrade on Tuesday minutes after Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic addressed a rally of his followers, witnesses said.
"The police is beating the (opposition) crowd and throwing tear gas. The crowd is going at the police," a witness said.

The fight was the latest in a series of fierce street battles in the capital in which a man was shot in the head and at least seven people were injured. Reporters said fights between supporters of the Zajedno opposition coalition and Milosevic's ruling socialists were breaking out in various parts of the city.
Tuesday's socialist demonstration meant to prop up Milosevic was dwarfed by a rival opposition rally and raised tensions to a fever pitch
Only 40,000 Socialist supporters, a fraction of those expected, turned out in a blow to Milosevic's attempts to quell 35 days of protests by the Zajedno parties who accuse him of election fraud.

A column of Zajedno supporters swelling to more than 200,000 in protest against the violence marched through central Belgrade as Milosevic spoke to the rally, his first public appearance since the crisis began.
